input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 matches the preferred position exactly: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience (in whole or in part) on thirty days' written notice, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no early-termination fee, and Vendor is expressly denied any convenience-termination right during a committed term. No other termination provision (§§ 9.1–9.5, 10.1–10.2, 24.4, 27.3) grants Vendor a convenience right or imposes an exit penalty on us, so nothing to redline. Note only: § 2.1's three-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" sits in tension with § 9.4's convenience right; that is a minimum-commitment issue and is raised under the MINCOMMIT rule rather than flagged twice here.
